answer: Each seat is backed by one pearl, not one key. An operator files a hatchery lot and the raft where the oyster grows, so the pearl carries a nacre record of its growth days. At the seasonal nadir of water temperature the registry scans that record without cutting the shell, then retires it: one pearl, one seat. A thousand cloned wallets on one raft still yield one pearl and fold into one seat. Extra seats mean extra lots, raft time through the cold months and per-pearl grading, while emission per seat stays flat. Shells grown on an open dune leave a nacre signature that fails the scan.
